EnTTRegistry.note: The EnTT registry a 1.26 Actor holds at +16 (the entity id is the dword at +24). Every inlined component lookup in the build walks it with the same instructions -- Actor::getEntityTypeId, Actor::getRuntimeID and Player::getAbilities are identical up to the component's size, on both builds -- so these are the offsets bdsx needs to do the lookup itself for the names 1.26 kept no out-of-line copy of (docs/findings-riding.md). poolsBegin/poolsEnd are the bucket array of the open-addressed map from entt::type_hash to storage; nodes/nodesEnd are its node array (32-byte nodes: next index at +0, the hash at +8, the storage pointer at +16, and nodesEnd is the end sentinel a hit is compared against); sparseBegin/sparseEnd are the storage's sparse pages and packed is its element pages at +80. entityBits 18 is the index half of an entt::entity, sparsePageBits 11 is 2048 entries per sparse page, packedPageBits 7 is 128 elements per packed page -- the same three constants for a 4-byte component (ActorTypeComponent), an 8-byte one (RuntimeIDComponent) and a 1464-byte one (AbilitiesComponent). entitySparseBegin/End (0xe0/0xe8) are the registry`s entity storage sparse page vector, what `registry.valid(entity)` walks: 2024's 0x2728b20 reads the same offsets, and a runtime scan of the live registry on both 1.26 builds finds exactly one (begin,end) pair that is a page vector holding the bot's id with the right version and rejecting a bumped version: +0xe0 (docs/findings-inventory.md section 16, ukscan). The 0x110/0x118 loads that look like it in the binary belong to another class.
